claim_title: SYSDATETIME() on the SQL Server container is UTC, not +07 — three clocks in the stack disagree
observations_verified_true: engflow-backend container date = 2026-09-22 03:54:52 +0700 (compose docker-compose.yml line 52 = 'TZ=Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh'; backend.Dockerfile line 14 ENV TZ and line 17 -Duser.timezone=Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh).
engflow-sqlserver container date = 2026-09-21 20:54:51 +0000; docker inspect shows NO TZ env var on the sqlserver container.

SELECT SYSDATETIME() = 2026-09-21 20:54:56.2829823; SYSUTCDATETIME() = 2026-09-21 20:54:56.2829823; SYSDATETIMEOFFSET() = 2026-09-21 20:54:56.2829823 +00:00; DATEDIFF(MINUTE, SYSDATETIME(), SYSUTCDATETIME()) = 0. The claim's raw clock facts are REAL and REPRODUCIBLE.
why_refuted: IMPACT MECHANISM ABSENT: zero usages of SYSDATETIME()/GETDATE()/GETUTCDATE()/CURRENT_TIMESTAMP in application source. grep -rhoiE over src/main/java/**/*.java = 0 occurrences. Zero native queries (grep nativeQuery src/main/java = 0 files). So no 'ad-hoc SYSDATETIME() comparison against a datetime2 column' exists anywhere in the app.

NO DB-SIDE CLOCK IS LIVE: sys.default_constraints count = 0 (ALL_DEFAULTS|0). The DEFAULT GETDATE() literals in db/migration/V1,V3,V9 never took effect in this DB — Flyway is disabled (spring.flyway.enabled=false) and Hibernate ddl-auto=update created the schema without them. sys.triggers = 0. No stored proc/function writes timestamps.

ALL TIMESTAMPS ARE WRITTEN BY THE JVM (+07): every entity uses @CreationTimestamp/@UpdateTimestamp (15 entities). Real HTTP write test: registered user via POST /api/auth/register at host-local 2026-09-22 03:56:56 +0700 -> stored users.created_at = 2026-09-22 03:56:56.5368774, i.e. the +07 wall clock, NOT UTC 20:56. Data is internally consistent +07 across users/speaking_submissions/video_attempts/lessons.

CLAIM'S DIRECTION IS WRONG: the claim states 'DATEDIFF(MINUTE,col,SYSDATETIME()) reports every stored timestamp 7h older than it is.' Empirically DATEDIFF(MINUTE, col, SYSDATETIME()) where col holds +07 local now = -420 (NEGATIVE), and on real data DATEDIFF(MINUTE, MAX(created_at), SYSDATETIME()) = -417. A local (+07) col appears 7h in the FUTURE relative to UTC SYSDATETIME(), not '7h older'. The stated sign is inverted.

EXPECTED BEHAVIOUR, NOT A BUG: the official mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server image runs the container in UTC by default (no TZ). The app correctly pins its own clock to +07 (compose + Dockerfile). This is a sound design; the 'three clocks disagree' framing describes standard container config, not a defect.
residual_valid_note: The one true, correctly-stated fact is that SYSDATETIME()/GETDATE() inside engflow-sqlserver returns UTC. That is a trap ONLY for a human/agent writing ad-hoc SQL (the existing probe scripts sweep/v8/db-audit.sql and sweep/v8/p6_db_audit_v9.sql already document and work around it). No application code path is affected. Warrants at most an INFO/docs note, not a LOW defect.
